title: 📦 The Colonel’s bow-tie and Amazon’s forgotten business
body_text: If you’ve ever found yourself contemplating your life choices – and the precise make up of the famously secret blend of 11 herbs and spices – after polishing off an 8-piece KFC bucket, an auction earlier this week in Shelbyville, Ky., may have held some partial answers. Harland Sanders’ personal planner from 1964 was sold at auction for $30,000, the Associated Press reports . Among its entries is a handwritten list of herbs and spices (KFC maintains the list does not match their near-dozen blend). Also hitting the auction block: a black clip-on ribbon bow tie worn by the non-military Colonel himself. That sartorial bit of culinary history ending up selling for $8,000. The S&P 500 dropped about 1.5% and the Nasdaq 100 fell just over 2%, enough for the latter to officially enter a correction , as the Federal Reserve held rates steady with three officials dissenting in favor of a rate hike. Following last night’s earnings from Meta and Microsoft and last week’s earnings from Google and Tesla , tonight we get the last round of earnings from the Magnificent Seven as Apple and Amazon tell us how the quarter went. The companies have taken very different approaches to the AI moment. Amazon, through its subsidiary AWS, has poured tens of billions and intends to pour hundreds of billions more into an AI buildout. Apple has ceded that data center race, but still has its bets on consumer products that stand to benefit from AI advancements. The numbers are staggering; Amazon’s looking at $200 billion in capital expenditures for 2026, while Apple’s looking at $13 billion to $14 billion , an order of magnitude less. Amazon, which is singlehandedly responsible for something like 30 percent of the combined AI infrastructure spend across Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, and Alphabet , is betting that that investment allows its cloud business to win the compute race. Apple waved the white flag on multiple segments of the AI business, a somewhat humiliating retreat for a company whose Siri was relatively early to market. That demoralizing and embarrassing retreat has [checks note] sent them up nearly 24% year to date? While Amazon is flat, Meta’s down 11%, and Microsoft is down 19%? Interesting. Apple has also managed to ride the AI wave thanks to its Apple Silicon chips, which have been in high demand for Mac Minis and hardware that can host consumer-grade and self-hosted models, with many of those out of stock for weeks or months amid the RAM crunch. Oh, wait, Amazon also runs a big store too, right? The AI conversation has been such a huge driver of stock movement over the past few quarters that at times we must remind ourselves that Amazon, the popular cloud services company, actually operates the second-largest retailer in America and the largest delivery provider by volume , seemingly as a side-hustle. Guess we’ll find out how that project’s going. Do you think Amazon, once a humble book store, would just have sold away all of those incredibly valuable AI training materials had they known their real value to the insatiable maw of AI training ? The S&P 500 rose slightly while the Nasdaq 100 dipped nearly one percent as oil’s decline continued to provide broad support to stocks, while the continued chip dip pushed tech shares lower. Meta and Microsoft — two of the largest and spendiest companies in the world — are slated to report earnings results after the close today at a time when investors are feeling increasingly queasy about the amounts Big Tech is spending on artificial intelligence. Last week, Google ’s parent reported capital expenditures above its previous forecast, making for its first cash-flow negative quarter since it went public in 2004. The company said its spending is aimed at meeting a growing backlog of cloud contracts. Still, that news dragged down other hyperscalers, including Meta and Microsoft, as well as the broader market. Microsoft is expected to keep its free cash flow in the green. Meanwhile, analysts are expecting Meta to report its first free cash-flow negative quarter since 2012. Here is what the two have guided for capex as of their last report: Microsoft — which will be reporting its fiscal Q4 results — said in its last report that it expects to spend $190 billion in capital expenditures this calendar year. Meta (whose fiscal calendar overlaps with the normal calendar year) set its guidance for 2026 capex at between $125 and 145 billion . I’m old enough to remember when investors were excited about big spending on capex, seeing it as both proof that a company is staying on the cutting edge and as a promise of future demand. Now they seem more eager to see money coming in, not out. “In our view, investors are becoming less willing to reward higher AI spending on its own and are increasingly looking for progress in earning a return on that investment,” said Brian Therien, a senior analyst at Edward Jones. Investors have more to look forward to on Thursday: Amazon and Apple , with the latter less exposed to AI anxieties than the former. 🚀 SpaceX: Last year, SpaceX launched 165 orbital flights . title: 💡 Marketplace of ideas
body_text: “Waiter, there’s an ant in my sorbet!” may sound like the start of a tired joke, but it’s actually the basis of a very serious and real criminal case in South Korea, where authorities arrested a top chef with two Michelin stars in connection with serving up ant-sprinkled desserts. Despite customers' awareness of the insects in their orders, prosecutors are reportedly seeking a one-year sentence for the chef and a 20 million won (~$14,000) fine for the Seoul restaurant, owing to the fact that ants aren’t one of the 10 insects approved for human consumption in South Korea. Whether you’re looking to furnish your new apartment with vintage furniture, hunting for an instrument to help finally realize your longstanding musical ambitions, or simply trying to offload the clothes that your kids (or you) have long grown out of, Facebook Marketplace has become one of the go-to platforms for buying and selling pre-loved goods. Now, Meta is making it even easier for the site’s sellers to make listings and manage their offers, announcing the “Seller” app at the end of last week. The new app comes with a dedicated suite of tools such as a built-in inbox, new AI listing capabilities, and listing performance analytics. Given Marketplace’s growth in recent years — it has ballooned to 430 million monthly listings and now counts 1.1 billion active users — it’s little wonder that Meta is looking to expand on one of the true business bright spots across its sprawling online empire. Per Google Trends data, search interest in Facebook Marketplace has soared far ahead of that for its Messenger platform in the US; it even overtook searches to login to the site overall in early 2023, as more Americans look to Marketplace to buy and sell online. Even though Marketplace has shone as a jewel in Meta’s internet crown for a while now (traffic was up 15% year-over-year in 2024, compared to a 3.6% decline across the broader Facebook.com domain), the carved-out app feels like a notable step up for the platform, expanding its position as an ecommerce behemoth and building on a partnership it announced with legacy industry titan eBay last year . 📺 Big Brother: Markets are currently pricing contestant Dee Valladares as the favorite to win “Big Brother” season 28 at an 18% chance of victory. * Other strong contenders include Barrett Pfeiffer (11%), Rick Devens (14%) and Kamu Kirk (10%). 🎬 Paramount: The news last week that Paramount agreed to delay its merger with Warner Bros. for “months” has upended markets that had for months been bullish on Paramount’s chances at completing the merger; the probability that nobody buys Warner jumped from 15% to 29% over the weekend . *Event contracts are offered through Robinhood Derivatives, LLC — probabilities referenced or sourced from KalshiEx LLC or ForecastEx LLC.
